samples.text:
The table shows how many men and women worked in five technology jobs in one country in 2024, and also the percentage of women in each job.

Overall, there were more men than women in all of the occupations, but in some jobs the difference were much smaller.

Software developers was the biggest occupation. There were 412 thousand men but only 98 thousand women, so women were just 19% of the total. IT support technicians was similar, with 188 thousand men and 44 thousand women, which is also 19%. Cyber-security specialists had the lowest percentage of women, only 18%, there were 73 thousand men and 16 thousand women.

On the other hand, data analysts and web and UX designers had more balance between men and women. In data analysts there were 96 thousand men and 71 thousand women, so women was 43%. Web and UX designers had 57 thousand men and 49 thousand women, and the percentage of women was 46%, which is the highest in the table.

In conclusion, men are the majority in technology jobs, especially in software and cyber-security.
samples.why: Relevant overview and accurate figures · occupations sensibly grouped but described mechanically · unnecessary concluding sentence · repetitive vocabulary · agreement errors and a comma splice that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The table compares the number of men and women working in five technology occupations in one country in 2024, and shows women's share of the total workforce in each.

Overall, men outnumbered women in every occupation. However, the gender gap was much narrower among data analysts and web and UX designers than in the other three jobs, where women made up less than a fifth of the workforce.

Software development was by far the largest occupation, employing 412 thousand men and just 98 thousand women, so women accounted for only 19% of software developers. The picture was similar for IT support technicians, with 188 thousand men compared with 44 thousand women, and again women represented 19%. Cyber-security had the lowest female share of all, at 18%, as there were 73 thousand male specialists but only 16 thousand female specialists.

By contrast, the numbers were far more balanced in the remaining two occupations. Among web and UX designers, there were 57 thousand men and 49 thousand women, giving the highest female proportion at 46%. Similarly, women made up 43% of data analysts, with 71 thousand women and 96 thousand men working in this field.
samples.why: Clear overview contrasting the two groups of occupations · key features highlighted with apt comparisons · logical paragraphing · good range of vocabulary · mostly error-free, with some repetitive phrasing.

samples.text:
The table provides a breakdown by sex of employment in five technology occupations in one country in 2024, with figures in thousands, and also indicates the proportion of each workforce made up of women.

Men were in the majority in all five occupations, but the degree of imbalance varied considerably. Women were most poorly represented in software development, IT support and cyber-security, while data analysis and web and UX design came much closer to parity.

Software development was the largest field by a wide margin, employing 412 thousand men, over four times the number of women (98 thousand). Women therefore accounted for just 19% of software developers, the same proportion as among IT support technicians, where 44 thousand women worked alongside 188 thousand men. Cyber-security, the smallest of the five occupations, had the lowest female share of all, at 18%, with only 16 thousand women compared with 73 thousand men.

The two remaining occupations presented a markedly different picture. Web and UX design was the most balanced, with 49 thousand women and 57 thousand men, meaning that women made up 46% of the workforce. Data analysis was only slightly less even, with 71 thousand women and 96 thousand men, giving a female share of 43%.
samples.why: Well-structured overview on the degree of imbalance · figures selected and compared precisely · cohesion and referencing handled smoothly · precise vocabulary (parity, breakdown) · wide range of accurate structures.
